sources.description:
The ADOT Broadband Office is responsible for administering the agency broadband program. Their goals are to Reduce Barriers, Maximize Resource Sharing and ITS (Intelligent Transportation Systems) Opportunities, and to Assist Statewide Broadband Initiatives to Expand Broadband and Connect AZ! The ADOT Broadband Office is committed to providing professional and quality service to the Department and its Customers, consistent with the Department’s goals and objectives in meeting the transportation needs of the State of Arizona.

Current broadband projects include I-17, I-19 & I-40. These projects are designed to be open-access, middle-mile broadband projects. Duraline armored 7-way multi-duct conduit is used, along with 3 pull boxes every 3,000 feet and a node building approximately every 50 miles. A neutral, third-party provider known as the OMC (Operate-Maintain-Commercialize) vendor, will be responsible for leasing fiber and ducts along the routes.

Contact the Broadband Office by email: broadband@azdot.gov

Visit https://azdot.gov/business/adot-broadband-office for current information and contacts.

sources.description:
This hosted feature layer contains multiple sublayers developed to support planning, environmental review, and public communication for the Pima County Regional Middle Mile broadband infrastructure project. The service includes: (1) an approximate proposed fiber route, (2) the Environmental Assessment (EA) study area used to evaluate potential environmental and cultural impacts, and (3) a 25-mile buffer around the route.

All datasets are intended for high-level visualization and public information only. The geometries shown are approximate and subject to change as project planning, engineering, permitting, and construction progress. This service does not represent final design alignments, surveyed locations, or legally binding project boundaries.
